text: This is Zybuu. We build infrastructure for AI workloads that have to stay under your control: software as a service, private cloud, or fully air-gapped. Abhed is our first product: an agent harness for work that cannot leave the building.

Every enterprise is going to run agents. Most are offered them one way: a vendor's cloud, the vendor's model, and your data leaving the building on every turn. Abhed runs where the data already lives, on any of twenty model providers, including the one on your own GPUs.

Here is a real run, captured, not mocked. A twenty-six billion parameter model on a laptop is asked to add a function, write a test, and run the suite. Watch the tool contract refuse a relative path, and the agent recover. Every step is recorded, and nothing left the machine.

Five guarantees, each one tested in the repository. It runs where the data is. It runs any model. It is sandboxed by default. Every action is on the record. And it embeds into your own software without weakening. We also say plainly what is not true yet: no certifications, no S L A, and a human red team still outstanding.
This is the Abhed console, a reference application built on the same S D K a customer would use. Accounts are issued, never self-served, and every session is scoped to a tenant.

Let's give it work. The agent reads the workspace inside its sandbox, and each tool call appears as it happens, with its arguments and its result. The transcript you are watching is the audit record itself, replayable step by step.

Writes are a permission, not a default. In the default mode a change waits for a person to approve it, and the decision is recorded with who made it. When a chat is no longer needed, delete it. The console removes it, and the append-only store notes who did so.

Access is issued, never self-served. The operator's dashboard shows who has access, who asked for it, and every revocation with its reason and an automatic email. The policy it enforces is public, in the documentation, and every admin route is checked on the server, so a link is only ever a link.
Documentation lives with the product: install, configuration, permissions, the S D K, structured output, parallel subagents with worktree isolation, and scheduled runs.
Abhed is invite-only today. Request access at zybuu dot com and we will get back to you the same day. Thanks for watching.
